info.title: g2way admin API
info.description: Control-plane API of the g2way gateway: key, API definition, and policy management, hot reload, and node status. Definition/policy writes go live on reload, not on write.

200.description: Every stored API definition, sorted by id

409.description: api_id already exists; use PUT to update

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The api_id; must equal the body's api_id

200.description: Stored; `action` is `added` or `modified` (live after the next reload)

400.description: Validation failed or body id disagrees with path id

post.summary:
`POST /g2/graphql/sync` — broadcast a GraphQL schema-sync nudge to
every gateway pod (this one included) via storage pub/sub.
post.description:
Returns as soon as the nudge is published: each pod immediately
re-fetches the schema of every API configuring `graphql.schema_sync`
from its upstream via introspection, swapping the compiled schema on
change and keeping the previous one on any failure (surfaced on
`GET /g2/node`). APIs without `schema_sync` are unaffected.

get.summary: `GET /g2/health` — unauthenticated liveness for probes on the admin port.
`GET /g2/keys` — list the organization's stored key hashes, sorted.
get.description:
Returns `{"keys": ["<hash>", …]}`. Hashes are the only listable handle:
raw keys are never stored. Takes an optional `?org_id=`.

parameters.name: hashed
parameters.description:
When `true`, the path parameter is the stored key hash itself
instead of a raw key.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description:
Organization the key belongs to (`GET`/`DELETE` only; `POST`/`PUT`
read it from the session body). Defaults to the single-org default.

post.summary: `POST /g2/keys` — create a session under a freshly generated key.
post.description:
The raw key is returned **only here**; it is stored hashed and cannot be
recovered later.

parameters.name: hashed
parameters.description:
When `true`, the path parameter is the stored key hash itself
instead of a raw key.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description:
Organization the key belongs to (`GET`/`DELETE` only; `POST`/`PUT`
read it from the session body). Defaults to the single-org default.

put.summary: `PUT /g2/keys/{key}` — create or update the session stored for `key`.

parameters.name: hashed
parameters.description:
When `true`, the path parameter is the stored key hash itself
instead of a raw key.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description:
Organization the key belongs to (`GET`/`DELETE` only; `POST`/`PUT`
read it from the session body). Defaults to the single-org default.

parameters.name: hashed
parameters.description:
When `true`, the path parameter is the stored key hash itself
instead of a raw key.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description:
Organization the key belongs to (`GET`/`DELETE` only; `POST`/`PUT`
read it from the session body). Defaults to the single-org default.

get.summary: `GET /g2/node` — node identity plus the APIs currently being routed.

200.description: Node identity, version, uptime, and the currently routed APIs
Every stored policy, sorted by id

409.description: policy_id already exists; use PUT to update

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The policy_id; must equal the body's policy_id

400.description: Validation failed or body id disagrees with path id

post.summary:
`POST /g2/reload` — broadcast a config-reload nudge to every gateway
pod (this one included) via storage pub/sub.
post.description:
Returns as soon as the nudge is published: reloads happen
asynchronously on each pod, which re-reads definitions from files and
storage, rebuilds its route table, and keeps the old table if the new
config fails to load (logged per pod).

get.summary: `GET /g2/stats` — per-API request counters since process start.

200.description: Per-API request and status-class counters (process-local, reset on restart)

get.summary:
`GET /g2/version` — the gateway's version (workspace-wide, so the crate
version equals the binary's).

`GET /metrics` — the gateway's metrics in the Prometheus text exposition
format (unauthenticated: scrapers do not send custom headers, and the
admin port is expected to stay off the public network).

200.description: Prometheus text exposition of the gateway's metrics

503.description: Metrics are not enabled on this node

ApiAccess.description:
Access granted to a single API.

An entry's presence in [`KeySession::access`] is the base grant; the
fields below add per-key GraphQL restrictions, enforced by the GraphQL
middleware on GraphQL-configured APIs
and ignored everywhere else. An empty `{}` entry — every pre-M9 record —
grants unrestricted access.

allowed_types.description:
GraphQL field allow list. When non-empty, the key may select **only**
the listed (type, field) pairs — and the block list is ignored (the
allow list wins). Empty = no allow-list restriction.

disable_introspection.description:
Disables GraphQL introspection (`__schema` / `__type`) for this key
on this API, even when the API itself allows it.

max_query_depth.description:
Per-key GraphQL depth limit override. `Some(n > 0)` replaces the
API's `graphql.max_query_depth` (even with a larger value);
`Some(-1)` (or any non-positive value) lifts the limit entirely
(`-1`); `None` inherits the API's limit.

restricted_types.description:
GraphQL field block list: selecting a listed (type, field) pair is
rejected with `400`. Consulted only while `allowed_types` is empty.

ApiDefinition.description:
One API proxied by the gateway.

This is the unit of configuration: requests whose path falls under
`listen_path` are forwarded to `target_url`.

Definitions come from two sources merged at load time (ADR-0002): files
(see [`crate::loader`]) and storage records under
[`api_definition_storage_key`], managed through the admin API.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "api_id": "httpbin",
  "name": "Httpbin passthrough",
  "listen_path": "/httpbin/",
  "target_url": "http://httpbin.default.svc.cluster.local"
}
```

active.description: Inactive definitions are loaded and listed but never routed to.

allow_ips.description:
When non-empty, only clients whose socket address matches one of
these IPs/CIDR networks may use this API; everyone else gets `403`.
The peer address is used, never client-supplied headers like
`X-Forwarded-For` (which are spoofable).

allow_paths.description:
When non-empty, only requests matching one of these rules are
forwarded; everything else on this API is rejected with `403` (the
API becomes allow-list-only). See [`crate::endpoints`] for the
evaluation order.

api_id.description: Unique, stable identifier for this API.

auth.description:
How clients authenticate. Defaults to token auth on the
`Authorization` header; keyless must be requested explicitly.

block_ips.description:
Clients whose socket address matches one of these IPs/CIDR networks
are rejected with `403`. A block always wins over `allow_ips`.

block_paths.description:
Requests matching one of these rules are rejected with `403`. A
block always wins: it applies even to paths that are also allowed,
ignored, or mocked.

oneOf.description:
Optional response caching: safe-method (`GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS`) `2xx`
upstream responses are stored in shared storage for a per-API TTL and
replayed without contacting the upstream (see [`CacheConfig`]).
Unset = no caching.

Optional per-route circuit breaking: after enough consecutive
upstream failures on live traffic, requests are answered `503`
without contacting the upstream until a cooldown trial succeeds (see
[`CircuitBreakerConfig`]). Unset = no breaking.

Optional CORS settings: when present the gateway answers preflight
requests and decorates responses with `Access-Control-*` headers
(see [`CorsConfig`]).

enable_upgrades.description:
When `true`, HTTP/1.1 `Connection: Upgrade` requests (WebSocket being
the common protocol) are passed through: the upgrade headers are
forwarded, and when the upstream answers `101 Switching Protocols` the
gateway tunnels the connection's raw bytes in both directions for its
remaining lifetime. The upgrade *request* still runs the full
middleware chain (auth, rate limits, path lists), but bytes inside an
established tunnel are opaque to the gateway. When `false` (the
default) the upgrade headers are stripped like any other hop-by-hop
header and the request is proxied as plain HTTP.

endpoint_rate_limits.description:
Aggregate per-endpoint rate limits: the first rule matching a
request caps how many matching requests **all clients combined** may
make per window; excess is rejected with `429`. Counted
independently of any key session's rate/quota and enforced even on
keyless APIs and `ignore_auth_paths` matches (see
[`EndpointRateLimit`]).

oneOf.description:
Optional GraphQL settings: present, the API is treated as a GraphQL
API — requests are parsed, validated against the configured schema,
and policed (depth limits, introspection control, per-key field
permissions) before being proxied (see [`GraphQlConfig`]).
Unset = plain HTTP proxying.

Optional active upstream health checking: each pod probes every
upstream address on an interval and evicts failing addresses from the
load-balancing rotation until they recover (see
[`HealthCheckConfig`]). Unset = no probing.

ignore_auth_paths.description:
Requests matching one of these rules skip authentication (and with
it session rate limiting, which needs a session) — e.g. a public
health or webhook endpoint on an otherwise protected API. API-level
[`endpoint_rate_limits`](Self::endpoint_rate_limits) still apply.

listen_path.description: URL path prefix the gateway listens on for this API. Must begin with `/`.

max_request_body_bytes.description:
Maximum request body size in bytes; larger requests are rejected
with `413`. Enforced on the `Content-Length` header and, for
chunked/streamed bodies, on the actual bytes read. Unset = no limit.

name.description: Human-readable name (shown in logs and the future dashboard).

org_id.description: Owning organization. Always [`DEFAULT_ORG_ID`] in single-org mode.

oneOf.description:
Optional WASM plugin hooks: guest modules run before authentication
(`pre`) and after authentication/rate limiting (`post`), able to
mutate request headers or answer the request themselves (see
[`PluginsConfig`]). Unset = no plugins.

preserve_host_header.description:
When `true`, the client's original `Host` header is forwarded upstream.
When `false` (the default), the upstream host from `target_url` is used.

oneOf.description:
Optional upstream service discovery: each pod polls an HTTP+JSON
endpoint on an interval and live-swaps the API's load-balancing
targets to the discovered addresses (see [`ServiceDiscoveryConfig`]).
[`Self::target_list`]/[`Self::target_url`] remain the seed addresses
used until the first successful poll. Unset = static targets only.

strip_listen_path.description:
When `true` (the default), the `listen_path` prefix is removed from the
request path before the request is forwarded upstream.

target_list.description:
Upstream base URLs for round-robin load balancing. When non-empty,
upstream requests rotate across these
URLs — each gateway pod keeps its own rotation — and [`Self::target_url`]
is not used for forwarding. Every entry follows `target_url`'s rules
and may carry its own base path.

target_url.description:
Base URL of the upstream service, e.g. `http://users.svc:8000/api`.
Must be an absolute `http`/`https` URL.

oneOf.description:
Optional minijinja body transforms for matching request and response
bodies (see [`BodyTransforms`]). Matching bodies are buffered whole —
requests up to [`max_request_body_bytes`](Self::max_request_body_bytes)
(else 1 MiB, over → `413`), responses up to the block's
`max_response_body_bytes` (over → `502`) — and transforms fail closed:
a failing render answers `500` (request) or `502` (response) rather
than passing the original body through. Templates see JSON-parsed
bodies only (`body` is `none` for non-JSON payloads; `raw` always
carries the text). Design: ADR-0007.

Optional header add/remove transforms applied to this API's
upstream-bound requests and client-bound responses.

transform_method.description:
Optional HTTP method override for upstream-bound requests (e.g.
`"POST"`, case-insensitive; `CONNECT` is not allowed). The body and
headers are forwarded unchanged, and gateway responses still describe
the client's original method.

upstream_http2.description:
When `true`, every upstream request for this API is sent over
HTTP/2: plaintext `http://` targets speak h2c (prior knowledge —
the upstream must accept HTTP/2 directly, there is no HTTP/1.1
fallback), and `https://` targets offer only `h2` via ALPN. This is
what makes gRPC passthrough work end to end (response trailers such
as `grpc-status` are forwarded), but it applies to *all* the API's
upstream traffic, gRPC or not. Cannot be combined with
[`Self::enable_upgrades`]: an HTTP/1.1 `Connection: Upgrade` cannot
cross an HTTP/2-only upstream connection. When `false` (the
default) upstream requests are HTTP/1.1.

upstream_retries.description:
Additional forwarding attempts after an upstream transport failure
(connection refused/reset — not timeouts or `5xx` responses), at most
`10`. Each attempt picks the next load-balancing address. Only
requests that can be safely replayed are retried: idempotent methods
(`GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `TRACE`, after any method
transform) whose body is empty — a streamed request body cannot be
re-sent. All attempts share the API's one `upstream_timeout_ms`
budget. Defaults to `0` (no retries).

upstream_timeout_ms.description:
Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the upstream response before
answering `504 Gateway Timeout`.

url_rewrites.description:
Regex URL rewrite rules, tried in order against the full client
request path; the first match decides the upstream path (see
[`UrlRewriteRule`]). Requests matching no rule follow the normal
listen-path strip/join.

oneOf.description:
Optional API versioning: the request header or query parameter that
selects a version, and per-version overrides applied on top of this
definition (see [`VersioningConfig`]). Unset = unversioned.
No authentication: every request is forwarded. Explicit opt-out.

Bearer/API-token auth: the token is looked up (hashed) in storage and
must resolve to a live [`KeySession`](crate::KeySession).

The token is searched in `header` first, then `query_param`, then
`cookie` (each only if configured).

cookie.description: Optional cookie name also accepted as a token carrier.

header.description:
Request header carrying the token. A `Bearer ` prefix, if present,
is stripped.

query_param.description: Optional query parameter also accepted as a token carrier.

oneOf.description:
JWT bearer auth: the token in `header` is verified against a static
key (or a key fetched from `jwks_url`) and its claims are turned into
an ephemeral session (no storage lookup).

header.description: Request header carrying the JWT (a `Bearer ` prefix is stripped).

identity_claim.description:
Claim used as the caller identity (session alias and rate-limit
key). Defaults to `sub`.

jwks_refresh_secs.description:
Seconds between background JWKS re-fetches. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_JWKS_REFRESH_SECS`]; only valid alongside `jwks_url`.

jwks_url.description:
URL of a JWKS document (RFC 7517 key set) to fetch RS256
verification keys from; tokens must carry a `kid` matching a key
in the set. Mutually exclusive with `public_key_pem`; rs256 only.

signing_method.description: Signature algorithm the tokens must use.

oneOf.description:
OIDC bearer auth: RS256 tokens issued by an external identity
provider are verified against keys discovered from `issuer_url`
(or fetched directly from `jwks_url`), with exact `iss` and `aud`
checks, and their claims are turned into an ephemeral session.

Optionally maps the OAuth2 client id (read from `policy_claim`) to a
stored [`Policy`](crate::Policy) via `policy_map`.

audiences.description:
Accepted `aud` values; required and non-empty (a deliberate
hardening choice). A token passes if its `aud`
intersects this list.

header.description:
Request header carrying the token (a `Bearer ` prefix is
stripped).

identity_claim.description:
Claim used as the caller identity (session alias and rate-limit
key). Defaults to `sub`.

issuer_url.description:
Identity provider issuer URL. Matched **byte-for-byte** against
the token's `iss` claim (a trailing-slash mismatch fails
closed, per OIDC), and used as the base of the discovery URL
`{issuer_url}/.well-known/openid-configuration` (one trailing
`/` is trimmed before concatenation only).

jwks_refresh_secs.description:
Seconds between background JWKS re-fetches. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_JWKS_REFRESH_SECS`].

jwks_url.description:
Direct JWKS URL, skipping OIDC discovery — for providers whose
discovery document is absent or non-standard.

policy_claim.description:
Claim holding the OAuth2 client id used for policy mapping.
Defaults to [`DEFAULT_OIDC_POLICY_CLAIM`] (`azp`); RFC 9068
access tokens may want `client_id` instead. (A single
configurable claim, not `aud`/`azp` heuristics.)

policy_map.description:
Client id → policy id. When non-empty, a token whose client id
is not mapped is rejected (deny-unmatched); when
empty (the default), tokens get a JWT-like ephemeral session
with access to this API only.

oneOf.description:
HTTP Basic auth (RFC 7617): `Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass)`.

The username resolves (hashed, under a `basic:` namespace) to a
stored [`KeySession`](crate::KeySession) whose
[`basic_auth`](crate::session::BasicAuthData) data carries the
bcrypt hash the presented password is verified against. Credentials
are read from the `Authorization` header only — never query or
cookie carriers, which would leak passwords into logs.

realm.description:
Realm advertised in the `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="…"`
challenge on 401 responses. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_BASIC_AUTH_REALM`].

oneOf.description:
Mutual-TLS auth: the client certificate the TLS handshake verified
is the credential.

The certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (see
[`session::cert_fingerprint_hex`](crate::session::cert_fingerprint_hex))
resolves — hashed, under an `mtls:` namespace — to a stored
[`KeySession`](crate::KeySession), provisioned via the admin key
CRUD as the raw key `mtls:{fingerprint}`. A certificate the CA
signed but nobody provisioned is rejected: transport-level
verification (the gateway's `tls.client_cert_mode`) and per-API
authorization are separate layers. Requires the gateway to
terminate TLS with `client_cert_mode: optional` or `required`; see
`docs/tls.md`.

HMAC request-signature auth (draft-cavage HTTP Signatures):
`Authorization: Signature keyId="…",algorithm="hmac-sha256",
headers="(request-target) date",signature="…"`.

The `keyId` resolves (hashed, under an `hmac:` namespace) to a stored
[`KeySession`](crate::KeySession) whose
[`hmac`](crate::session::HmacData) data carries the shared secret the
signature is verified with; provisioning is the admin key CRUD with
the raw key `hmac:{keyId}`. Credentials are read from the
`Authorization` header only (where the `Signature` scheme lives).

allowed_algorithms.description:
Algorithms accepted from the `Signature` header. Defaults to all
three SHA-2 variants; `hmac-sha1` is deliberately unsupported.

allowed_clock_skew_secs.description:
Maximum seconds the request's `Date` header may differ from the
gateway clock. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_HMAC_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS`]; an
explicit `null` disables the check. While enabled, `date` must be
among the signed headers (an unsigned `Date` is
attacker-controlled, so a skew check on it would prove nothing).

Never skip-serialized: `null` is a meaningful third state
(disabled), distinct from absent (default 300).

AuthConfig.description:
How clients authenticate to one API.

The default is [`AuthConfig::AuthToken`] reading the `Authorization`
header: an API is protected unless its definition **explicitly** opts out
with `{"auth": {"mode": "keyless"}}`. Forgetting to configure auth must
never silently expose an upstream.

BasicAuthData.description:
Basic-auth credential data attached to a session.

Present only on sessions addressed by a username (basic-auth mode); the
presented password is verified against `password_hash` on every request.

password_hash.description:
bcrypt hash of the user's password (a full `$2b$…` hash string).
The plaintext password is never persisted.

BodyTransformRule.description:
One body-transform rule: requests (or responses) matching it have their
body replaced by the rendered `template`.

The template is minijinja (Jinja2 syntax), inline in the definition —
there is no file/blob mode (a deliberate simplification: definitions
stay self-contained). It renders against `body` (the payload parsed as
JSON, `none` when it does not parse), `raw` (the payload as a lossy UTF-8
string) and `_g2` (request metadata: `method`, `path`, `query`,
`headers`, `session`, plus `status` for response rules).

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "pattern": "^/users/orders$",
  "methods": ["POST"],
  "template": "{\"order\": {{ body.id | tojson }}, \"src\": \"g2\"}",
  "content_type": "application/json"
}
```

content_type.description:
`Content-Type` set on the transformed message. Defaults to
`application/json`.

methods.description: Methods the rule applies to (case-insensitive). Empty = every method.

pattern.description: Regex searched against the full client request path.

template.description: The minijinja template whose rendered output replaces the body.

max_response_body_bytes.description:
Cap on a buffered upstream response body; a matching response larger
than this is rejected with `502` (transforms fail closed). Defaults
to 1 MiB. Request bodies are capped by the API's
`max_request_body_bytes` (same 1 MiB default) instead.

request.description: Rules for upstream-bound request bodies. First match wins.

response.description:
Rules for client-bound response bodies, matched on the *request's*
method and path. First match wins.

CacheConfig.description:
Response caching for one API (see [`ApiDefinition::cache`]).

The gateway caches upstream responses in storage (shared by every pod)
under [`response_cache_key_prefix`] and answers repeat requests without
contacting the upstream, marking them with an `x-g2-cache: hit` header.

What is cached is deliberately conservative:

- **Safe methods only** (`GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`). Each method
  caches separately.
- **`2xx` responses only**, and never a response carrying `Set-Cookie`:
  the cache is shared across clients and keys, so a
  per-client response must never be replayed to someone else.
- Bodies larger than `max_body_bytes` are passed through uncached.

Entries are keyed by the exact request method, path, and query (no
normalization: `?a=1&b=2` and `?b=2&a=1` cache separately) and expire
after `ttl_secs`. HTTP cache-control semantics (`Vary`, `no-store`,
`Age`) are not interpreted — the TTL is the whole contract.

GraphQL traffic (`POST`) is never cached here; `graphql.cache` reuses
this config shape for operation-keyed caching instead (ADR-0012).

max_body_bytes.description:
Largest response body (in bytes) worth caching; bigger responses are
streamed through uncached. Defaults to 1 MiB.

ttl_secs.description:
Seconds a cached response is served before it expires. Defaults to
`60`.

CircuitBreakerConfig.description:
Per-route circuit breaking on live traffic (see
[`ApiDefinition::circuit_breaker`]).

Each gateway pod counts consecutive upstream failures — transport errors,
upstream timeouts, and `5xx` upstream responses — for the route. After
`failure_threshold` consecutive failures the circuit *opens*: requests are
rejected with `503` without contacting the upstream for `cooldown_ms`.
The first request after the cooldown is let through as a trial
(*half-open*): its success closes the circuit, its failure re-opens it
for another cooldown. Any upstream success resets the failure count.

A deliberate design choice: rather than a rate-based breaker
(`threshold_percent` over `samples`, per endpoint), this one counts
consecutive failures per route, which needs no sliding sample window and
stays lock-free on the hot path. State is pod-local, like load-balancing
rotation and health eviction.

cooldown_ms.description:
Milliseconds the circuit stays open before a trial request is let
through. Defaults to `30000`.

failure_threshold.description:
Consecutive upstream failures after which the circuit opens.
Defaults to `5`.

CorsConfig.description:
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing settings for one API.

When configured, the gateway answers preflight `OPTIONS` requests itself
(unless `options_passthrough` is set) and decorates responses — gateway
rejections like `401`/`429` included, so browsers can read them — with
the appropriate `Access-Control-*` headers. Requests from origins not
listed here are still forwarded, just without CORS headers: enforcement
is the browser's job, access control is the IP/path lists' and auth's.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "allowed_origins": ["https://app.example.com"],
  "allowed_methods": ["GET", "POST", "DELETE"],
  "allowed_headers": ["Authorization", "Content-Type"],
  "allow_credentials": true,
  "max_age_secs": 600
}
```

allow_credentials.description:
Whether `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is sent. Requires
explicit `allowed_origins` (the wildcard is rejected — browsers
refuse that combination anyway).

allowed_headers.description:
Request headers advertised to preflight requests. Empty (the
default) mirrors whatever headers the preflight asks for.

allowed_methods.description:
Methods advertised to preflight requests. Defaults to the
CORS-safelisted methods ([`DEFAULT_CORS_METHODS`]).

allowed_origins.description:
Origins allowed to make cross-origin requests, e.g.
`https://app.example.com` (scheme, host, optional port — no path).
The single entry `"*"` allows every origin, but cannot be combined
with other origins or with `allow_credentials`.

exposed_headers.description:
Response headers browsers may expose to cross-origin scripts
(`Access-Control-Expose-Headers`).

max_age_secs.description:
Seconds browsers may cache a preflight result
(`Access-Control-Max-Age`). Omitted from responses when unset.

options_passthrough.description:
When `true`, preflight `OPTIONS` requests are forwarded to the
upstream instead of being answered by the gateway. Responses are
still decorated.

EndpointRateLimit.description:
One API-level endpoint rate limit: the first rule matching a request caps
how many matching requests **all clients combined** may make per window.

Counters are aggregate — they are not tied to any key session, so the
limit also protects keyless APIs and `ignore_auth_paths` matches. Excess
requests are rejected with `429` and the usual `X-RateLimit-*` headers.
Rules are tried in order; only the first match is checked and consumed.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "pattern": "^/users/search",
  "methods": ["POST"],
  "rate": { "requests": 10, "per_seconds": 60 }
}
```

methods.description: Methods the rule applies to (case-insensitive). Empty = every method.

pattern.description: Regex searched against the full client request path.

rate.description: The aggregate allowance for matching requests, across all clients.

GraphQlConfig.description:
GraphQL settings for one API (see [`ApiDefinition::graphql`]).

Present on a definition, the API is treated as a GraphQL API: requests
are parsed as GraphQL, validated against [`schema`](Self::schema), and
policed (depth limits, introspection control, per-key field permissions
from [`ApiAccess`](crate::session::ApiAccess)) before being forwarded.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "schema": "type Query { hello: String }",
  "max_query_depth": 8,
  "introspection_enabled": false,
  "playground": { "path": "/playground" }
}
```

[`ApiDefinition::graphql`]: crate::ApiDefinition::graphql

oneOf.description:
GraphQL-aware response caching (ADR-0012). When set, responses to
**query** operations are cached — keyed on the active schema, the
operation name, the query text, and the variables — and repeat
queries are answered without contacting the upstream (or re-running
gateway-side execution), marked `x-g2-cache: hit`. Mutations and
subscriptions always bypass, and a response carrying GraphQL
`errors` is never stored. The cache is shared across clients like
[`ApiDefinition::cache`](crate::ApiDefinition::cache); per-key
grants are re-checked on every request before the cache is read.
Unset = GraphQL responses are not cached.

data_sources.description:
Universal Data Graph data sources, keyed `"<RootType>.<field>"`
(e.g. `"Query.user"` — the schema's actual root operation type
names). Required (and only allowed) when
[`execution_mode`](Self::execution_mode) is
[`Udg`](GraphQlExecutionMode::Udg); every field of the query and
mutation root types must be mapped (ADR-0010).

enabled.description:
Kill switch: `false` disables all GraphQL handling for the API while
keeping the configuration in place (the config is still validated).
Defaults to `true`.

execution_mode.description:
How the gateway executes GraphQL. Defaults to (and currently only
supports) [`GraphQlExecutionMode::Proxy`].

introspection_enabled.description:
Whether introspection queries (`__schema` / `__type`) are allowed.
Defaults to `true`; keys can additionally disable introspection for
themselves via
[`ApiAccess::disable_introspection`](crate::session::ApiAccess::disable_introspection).

max_query_depth.description:
Maximum query depth (nested selection-set levels; `{ a { b } }` is
depth 2). Deeper queries are rejected with `403`.
Unset = unlimited; keys can override via
[`ApiAccess::max_query_depth`](crate::session::ApiAccess::max_query_depth).

persisted_queries.description:
Persisted GraphQL-as-REST endpoints: REST-shaped routes the gateway
answers by building a GraphQL request server-side. Matched in
order; the first match wins.

oneOf.description:
Optional gateway-served GraphiQL playground for this API. The page
sits behind the API's full middleware chain, so a protected API's
playground requires credentials.

schema.description:
The API's GraphQL schema in SDL form; validated with apollo-compiler
at write/load time. Incoming queries are validated against it — an
unknown field or type never reaches the upstream. Required in every
execution mode except `supergraph`, where it must be **empty**: the
supergraph schema is composed from
[`supergraph`](Self::supergraph), never authored (ADR-0011).

oneOf.description:
Periodic schema sync from upstream introspection. When set, each
gateway pod polls the upstream's introspection endpoint and swaps
the schema it validates against in memory (stale-on-error;
[`schema`](Self::schema) stays required as the seed). Unset = the
schema is static (ADR-0008).

GraphQL subscriptions over WebSocket. When set (and enabled), the
gateway accepts `graphql-transport-ws` / `graphql-ws` WebSocket
handshakes on the listen path and polices every subscribe operation
like an HTTP query (ADR-0009). Unset = WebSocket handshakes on the
GraphQL endpoint are rejected.

Federation supergraph settings. Required (and only allowed) when
[`execution_mode`](Self::execution_mode) is
[`Supergraph`](GraphQlExecutionMode::Supergraph) (ADR-0011).

GraphQlExecutionMode.description: How the gateway executes GraphQL for an API.

HeaderTransform.description:
Header add/remove rules for one direction (request or response).

`remove` runs before `add`, and `add` replaces any existing value — so a
name appearing in both ends up set to the `add` value, and adding an
already-present header overwrites it rather than appending.

add.description:
Headers to set on the message: name → literal value. An existing
header of the same name is replaced.

remove.description: Header names to remove from the message (applied before `add`).

request.description: Rules applied to the upstream-bound request.

response.description: Rules applied to the client-bound response.

HealthCheckConfig.description:
Active upstream health checking with eviction (see
[`ApiDefinition::health_check`]).

Each gateway pod probes every upstream address of the API on a fixed
interval with `GET {address base path}{path}`; only a `2xx` answer within
`timeout_ms` counts as healthy. An address failing `unhealthy_threshold`
consecutive probes is evicted from the load-balancing rotation until it
passes `healthy_threshold` consecutive probes again.

Eviction never empties the pool: when every address is evicted, requests
fall back to the plain rotation (a dead upstream then answers `502`
exactly like an unchecked one), so probing a single-target API observes
health without ever refusing traffic.

healthy_threshold.description:
Consecutive probe successes after which an evicted address rejoins
the rotation. Defaults to `2`.

interval_ms.description: Milliseconds between probe rounds (per pod). Defaults to `10000`.

path.description:
Path probed on each upstream address, joined onto the address's own
base path. Must start with `/`; defaults to
[`DEFAULT_HEALTH_CHECK_PATH`]. May carry a query string.

timeout_ms.description:
Milliseconds a probe may take before counting as a failure.
Defaults to `2000`.

unhealthy_threshold.description:
Consecutive probe failures after which an address is evicted from
the rotation. Defaults to `3`.

HmacAlgorithm.description:
HMAC digest algorithms supported by [`AuthConfig::Hmac`].

Serialized with the draft-cavage wire names (`hmac-sha256`, …), which are
also what the `Signature` header's `algorithm` parameter carries.
`hmac-sha1` is deliberately unsupported (a hardening choice).

HmacData.description:
HMAC signing credentials attached to a session.

Present only on sessions addressed by a `keyId` (hmac mode); each
request's `Signature` header is verified against `secret`.

secret.description:
Shared secret, HMAC'd as its raw UTF-8 bytes (so ordinary client
snippets work verbatim; arbitrary binary secrets are not supported). Unlike a
bcrypt hash, this is a live credential stored in plaintext — HMAC
verification needs the secret itself.

KeySession.description:
The state attached to one API key.

Sessions are created through the admin API (or seeded directly in
storage), persisted as JSON under [`session_storage_key`], and looked up
by auth middleware on every request carrying the key.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "alias": "acme-mobile-app",
  "rate": { "requests": 100, "per_seconds": 60 },
  "quota": { "max": 10000, "renewal_rate_secs": 3600 },
  "expires_at": 1790000000,
  "access": { "httpbin": {} }
}
```

access.description:
APIs this key may call, keyed by `api_id`. An **empty map grants
access to every API in the organization** (the behavior for keys
without access rights).

active.description: Inactive sessions fail auth without being deleted (a soft revoke).

alias.description:
Optional human-readable label, shown in logs and analytics in place
of the (hashed, unreadable) key.

apply_policies.description:
Policies applied to this key (see [`crate::Policy`]). When
non-empty, the referenced policy's rate/quota/access **replace**
this session's own at auth time ([`Self::apply_policy`]).

A `Vec` for forward compatibility, but currently at most one entry
(enforced by [`Self::validate`]); combining multiple policies needs
partitioned policies, a later refinement.

oneOf.description:
Basic-auth credentials, set only on sessions used with the
basic-auth mode. `None` means this session cannot authenticate via
basic auth.

expires_at.description:
Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the key stops working.
`None` means the key never expires.

oneOf.description:
HMAC signing credentials, set only on sessions used with the hmac
mode. `None` means this session cannot authenticate via request
signatures.

org_id.description: Owning organization. Always [`DEFAULT_ORG_ID`] in single-org mode.

oneOf.description: Long-period usage quota. `None` means unlimited.
Request-rate allowance. `None` means unlimited.

MockResponse.description:
One mock-response rule: requests matching it are answered by the gateway
itself, without contacting the upstream.

Rules are tried in order; the first match wins. The response carries
exactly the configured `status`, `headers` and `body` — no content type
is implied, set one in `headers` when the body needs it.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "pattern": "^/users/ping$",
  "methods": ["GET"],
  "status": 200,
  "body": "{\"pong\":true}",
  "headers": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
}
```

body.description: Literal response body. Defaults to empty.

methods.description: Methods the rule applies to (case-insensitive). Empty = every method.

pattern.description: Regex searched against the full client request path.

status.description: HTTP status of the mock response. Defaults to `200`.

PathRule.description:
One path-matching rule in an allow/block/ignore list.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{ "pattern": "^/users/internal/", "methods": ["POST", "DELETE"] }
```

methods.description: Methods the rule applies to (case-insensitive). Empty = every method.

pattern.description: Regex searched against the full client request path.

PersistedQuery.description:
One persisted GraphQL-as-REST endpoint.

A request matching `method` + `path` (relative to the listen path) is
rewritten by the gateway into a `POST` of `operation` to the upstream
GraphQL endpoint, with `variables` filled from the template below. The
persisted operation is subject to the same protections (depth,
introspection, field permissions) as a client-written query.

# Variable templating

`variables` must be a JSON object. String values are substituted:

- `"$path.<name>"` — the value of the `{<name>}` segment of `path`.
- `"$header.<name>"` — the value of request header `<name>` (JSON
  `null` when the header is absent).

Substitution recurses into nested objects and arrays; all other values
are passed through verbatim.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/users/{id}",
  "operation": "query User($id: ID!) { user(id: $id) { name } }",
  "variables": { "id": "$path.id" }
}
```

method.description:
HTTP method the endpoint answers (case-insensitive; `CONNECT` is not
allowed).

operation.description:
The GraphQL executable document sent upstream. Validated against the
API's schema at write/load time.

operation_name.description:
Operation to execute when `operation` defines several. Must name an
operation in the document; required in that case.

path.description:
Path relative to the API's listen path. Must start with `/`. A
segment of the form `{name}` matches any single segment and binds it
for `$path.<name>` substitution; names must be unique.

variables.description:
Variables template (a JSON object; see the type-level docs for the
`$path.` / `$header.` substitution rules). Unset = no variables.

PlaygroundConfig.description: Settings for the gateway-served GraphQL playground.

path.description:
Path the playground page is served on, relative to the API's listen
path. Must start with `/`; defaults to [`DEFAULT_PLAYGROUND_PATH`].

PluginRef.description: One plugin in a hook list: a guest module plus its instance settings.

config.description: Arbitrary JSON handed to the guest verbatim on every invocation.

max_memory_bytes.description:
Linear-memory cap per invocation in bytes
(default [`DEFAULT_MAX_MEMORY_BYTES`]).

name.description: Name used in logs and error messages.

path.description:
Path of the `.wasm` module, relative to the gateway's `plugins_dir`.
Absolute paths and `..` components are rejected.

timeout_ms.description:
Wall-clock budget per invocation in milliseconds
(default [`DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`], at most [`MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`]).

post.description: Hooks run after authentication and rate limiting, in order.

pre.description: Hooks run before authentication, in order.

Policy.description:
A reusable bundle of rate, quota, and API access settings.

When a key references a policy, the policy's `rate`, `quota`, and
`access` **replace** the session's own wholesale (non-partitioned
policy semantics; partitioned policies, which override selectively, are
a possible later refinement). Per-key state — expiry, active flag,
alias, basic-auth credentials — is never touched by a policy.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "policy_id": "free-tier",
  "name": "Free tier",
  "rate": { "requests": 10, "per_seconds": 60 },
  "quota": { "max": 1000, "renewal_rate_secs": 86400 },
  "access": { "httpbin": {} }
}
```

access.description:
APIs referencing keys may call, keyed by `api_id`. An **empty map
grants access to every API in the organization** (same rule as
[`KeySession::access`](crate::KeySession::access)).

active.description:
An inactive policy denies every key that references it (a soft kill
switch for a whole tier of keys).

name.description: Human-readable name (shown in logs and the future dashboard).

org_id.description: Owning organization. Always [`DEFAULT_ORG_ID`] in single-org mode.

policy_id.description: Unique, stable identifier keys reference in `apply_policies`.

oneOf.description:
Long-period usage quota granted to referencing keys. `None` means
unlimited.

Request-rate allowance granted to referencing keys. `None` means
unlimited.

Quota.description:
A long-period usage quota: at most `max` requests per renewal period.

Unlike [`RateLimit`] (a smoothing limit over seconds or minutes), a quota
is a billing-style allowance over hours or days. The live counter and its
reset timestamp are kept in storage (milestone M3), not on the session.

max.description: Maximum number of requests allowed inside one renewal period.

renewal_rate_secs.description:
Length of the renewal period in seconds (for example `3600` for an
hourly quota).

RateLimit.description: A request-rate allowance: at most `requests` per `per_seconds` window.

per_seconds.description: Length of the sliding window in seconds.

requests.description: Maximum number of requests allowed inside one window.

SchemaSyncConfig.description:
Schema-sync settings: how a pod fetches the upstream's schema via
GraphQL introspection (see [`GraphQlConfig::schema_sync`]).

The introspection `POST` goes to the API's own upstream (respecting
load balancing, service discovery, and health eviction) unless
[`url`](Self::url) points elsewhere. Every failure — transport, non-2xx,
invalid introspection JSON, a converted schema that does not compile, or
a persisted query invalid against the new schema — keeps the previous
schema serving and is surfaced on `GET /g2/node`.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "interval_ms": 300000,
  "headers": { "authorization": "Bearer token" }
}
```

headers.description:
Extra headers on the introspection request (upstream auth): name →
literal value. Hop-by-hop headers are rejected.

interval_ms.description:
Milliseconds between introspection fetches (must be > 0). Defaults
to [`DEFAULT_SCHEMA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS`]. An admin-triggered sync
(`POST /g2/graphql/sync`) fetches immediately regardless.

timeout_ms.description:
Per-fetch timeout in milliseconds (must be > 0). Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_SCHEMA_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS`].

url.description:
Absolute `http(s)` URL to introspect instead of the API's upstream —
for when introspection is served elsewhere (e.g. an internal
endpoint while the public one has introspection disabled).

ServiceDiscoveryConfig.description:
Upstream service discovery via HTTP+JSON polling (see
[`ApiDefinition::service_discovery`]).

Each gateway pod polls `endpoint` every `interval_ms` and extracts the
current upstream addresses from the JSON response using the configured
data paths (see [`Self::extract_entries`] for the exact semantics — the
mechanism covers Consul/etcd/Eureka-style REST catalogs with one shape).
A successful poll that yields a *different* address list replaces the
API's load-balancing targets live, without a reload.

Until the first successful poll the API forwards to its static seeds
(`target_list`, else `target_url` — which stays required as the
canonical fallback). A failed poll — fetch error, non-2xx, unparseable
body, extraction error, invalid entry, or an *empty* result — keeps the
previous addresses and logs a warning: stale targets beat empty targets,
so discovery can never leave an API with nothing to forward to.

Polling is pod-local (each pod polls the endpoint itself, like health
probing); the discovery endpoint is fetched over HTTP/1.1 regardless of
the API's `upstream_http2` setting, and response bodies are capped at
1 MiB.

data_path.description:
Dotted path to the host entry (or list of host entries) inside the
JSON response — e.g. `"Address"` or `"node.ip"`. Segments index
object keys, or array elements when they parse as a number. Empty
(the default) means the looked-up value itself.

endpoint.description:
The URL polled for the current upstream addresses. Must be an
absolute `http`/`https` URL.

interval_ms.description: Milliseconds between polls (per pod). Defaults to `10000`.

parent_data_path.description:
Optional dotted path to a JSON *array* to iterate: per element,
[`Self::data_path`] and [`Self::port_data_path`] are resolved
relative to the element instead of the response root. Empty means
the response root itself is the array (e.g. Consul's
`/v1/catalog/service/{name}`). Unset = no iteration; the paths
resolve from the root.

port_data_path.description:
Optional dotted path to the port for each host entry. The value must
be an integer `1`–`65535` or a string of digits. Unset = discovered
entries carry their own port or use the scheme default.

scheme.description:
Scheme (`http` or `https`) applied to discovered `host[:port]`
entries. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_DISCOVERY_SCHEME`]. Entries that are
already full `http(s)://` URLs keep their own scheme.

timeout_ms.description:
Milliseconds a poll may take before counting as a failure.
Defaults to `5000`.

SubgraphConfig.description: One subgraph of a federation supergraph.

headers.description:
Extra headers on every fetch to this subgraph (upstream auth): name
→ literal value. Hop-by-hop headers are rejected.

max_response_bytes.description:
Cap on a response body in bytes (must be > 0). Unset =
[`DEFAULT_UDG_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`].

name.description:
Unique name of the subgraph — used in composition errors and in the
field errors clients see when a subgraph fetch fails (upstream URLs
are never exposed).

sdl.description:
The subgraph's federation SDL (`@key` and friends), pasted into the
definition so composition is deterministic and validated at write
time (ADR-0011).

timeout_ms.description:
Per-fetch timeout in milliseconds (must be > 0). Unset = the API's
`upstream_timeout_ms`.

url.description: Absolute `http(s)` URL of the subgraph's GraphQL endpoint.

SubscriptionsConfig.description:
GraphQL-subscriptions-over-WebSocket settings (see
[`GraphQlConfig::subscriptions`]).

The gateway terminates the WebSocket subprotocol on both legs: client
`subscribe`/`start` payloads are validated against the schema and the
per-key grants before being forwarded; violations are answered with
protocol-level `error` messages and never reach the upstream. Upstream
frames are relayed verbatim. Requires the schema to define a
`Subscription` root type.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{ "max_message_bytes": 262144 }
```

enabled.description:
Kill switch inside the block; defaults to `true` (presence of the
block enables subscriptions, like [`GraphQlConfig::playground`]).

max_message_bytes.description:
Cap on a single client→gateway WebSocket message (must be > 0).
Unset = the API's `max_request_body_bytes`, else 1 MiB — the same
bound the HTTP-side body buffering uses.

subgraphs.description: The subgraphs to compose, in composition order. At least one.

TypeFields.description:
One GraphQL type and the fields of it a grant refers to.

Used by the allow/block lists of [`ApiAccess`]. A `fields` entry of
`"*"` refers to every field of the type, current and future
(non-recursive — it does not cascade into nested types).

fields.description: Field names of the type; `"*"` means every field.

allOf.description: A REST/JSON endpoint: the response body is the field's JSON value.

oneOf.description: A REST/JSON endpoint: the response body is the field's JSON value.

allOf.description:
An upstream GraphQL service: the gateway sends the root field's
sub-selection as a standalone query and merges the response.

oneOf.description:
An upstream GraphQL service: the gateway sends the root field's
sub-selection as a standalone query and merges the response.

UdgDataSource.description:
One Universal Data Graph data source (see
[`GraphQlConfig::data_sources`]): where the gateway fetches the value of
one root field in UDG mode.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{ "kind": "rest", "url": "http://users.internal/users/{{ args.id }}" }
```

UdgGraphQlSource.description:
A GraphQL data source for one UDG root field.

The gateway prints the requested field (selection set, aliases, and
arguments verbatim) together with the fragment definitions and variable
definitions its subtree uses, and `POST`s
`{"query": …, "variables": …}` to [`url`](Self::url). The response's
`data.<field>` becomes the field's value; its `errors` are appended to
the stitched response (message-only).

headers.description:
Extra headers on the fetch: name → value template (upstream auth).
Hop-by-hop headers are rejected.

max_response_bytes.description:
Cap on the response body in bytes (must be > 0). Unset =
[`DEFAULT_UDG_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`].

timeout_ms.description:
Per-fetch timeout in milliseconds (must be > 0). Unset = the API's
`upstream_timeout_ms`.

url.description:
Absolute `http(s)` URL of the upstream GraphQL endpoint (not
templated).

UdgRestSource.description:
A REST data source for one UDG root field.

`url`, header values, and `body` are minijinja templates (ADR-0007's
engine), rendered per request against
`{ args, _g2: { method, path, headers, session: { alias } } }` where
`args` are the coerced GraphQL field arguments. The rendered URL must be
absolute `http(s)`. The response body is parsed as JSON and becomes the
field's value; nested selections are projected from it.

body.description:
Optional request-body template. Sent with
`content-type: application/json` unless [`headers`](Self::headers)
overrides it.

headers.description:
Extra headers on the fetch: name → value template. Hop-by-hop
headers are rejected.

max_response_bytes.description:
Cap on the response body in bytes (must be > 0). Unset =
[`DEFAULT_UDG_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`].

method.description:
HTTP method of the fetch (case-insensitive; `CONNECT` is not
allowed). Defaults to `GET`.

timeout_ms.description:
Per-fetch timeout in milliseconds (must be > 0). Unset = the API's
`upstream_timeout_ms`.

url.description:
URL template. Rendered per request; the result must be an absolute
`http(s)` URL.

UrlRewriteRule.description:
One regex URL rewrite rule for an API.

Rules live on an [`ApiDefinition`](crate::ApiDefinition) as
`url_rewrites` and are tried in order; the first whose `pattern` matches
wins, and a request matching no rule is forwarded with the normal
listen-path strip/join.

- `pattern` is a regex searched (unanchored — anchor with `^`/`$` as
  needed) against the **full client request path**, listen path
  included, before any stripping.
- `rewrite` is the replacement template producing the upstream path:
  `$1`/`${name}` expand capture groups (`$$` is a literal `$`; a group
  that did not participate expands to the empty string). It must start
  with `/` and replaces the listen-path strip — the result is joined
  onto the target URL's base path exactly like a stripped tail. It may
  carry its own query string (`/new?flag=1`); the client's query is
  appended after it.

# Example (JSON)

```json
{ "pattern": "^/users/(\\d+)/profile$", "rewrite": "/profiles/$1" }
```

pattern.description: Regex searched against the full client request path.

rewrite.description: Replacement template for the upstream path (must start with `/`).

VersionLocation.description: Where the requested version name is read from.

VersionOverrides.description:
Per-version overrides applied on top of the base definition.

Every field is optional: present replaces the base value wholesale,
absent inherits it. `Option`-typed base fields (`transform_headers`,
`transform_method`) can be overridden but not cleared per version — keep
them off the base definition if only some versions want them.

allow_paths.description: Replacement allow-path rules for this version.

block_paths.description: Replacement block-path rules for this version.

oneOf.description:
Replacement response-cache settings for this version. Each version
caches under its own scope, so versions never share entries.
Replacement circuit-breaker settings for this version.

enable_upgrades.description:
Replacement `Connection: Upgrade` passthrough flag for this version
(`false` disables upgrade tunneling for the version).

endpoint_rate_limits.description:
Replacement endpoint rate limits for this version (replaced
wholesale). Each version's counters live under their own scope, so
versions never share allowances.

expires_at.description:
Unix time (seconds) after which this version is expired: requests for
it are rejected with `403`. The boundary is inclusive, like key
session expiry. Unset means the version never expires.

oneOf.description:
Replacement GraphQL settings for this version (schema, protections,
playground, persisted queries — replaced wholesale).
Replacement upstream health-check settings for this version.

ignore_auth_paths.description: Replacement ignore-auth-path rules for this version.

mock_responses.description: Replacement mock-response rules for this version.

oneOf.description:
Replacement WASM plugin hooks for this version (both hook lists —
replaced wholesale).

Replacement service-discovery settings for this version (replaced
wholesale). Like other `Option`-typed base fields it can be
overridden but not cleared per version — keep discovery off the base
definition if only some versions want it. The version's effective
`target_list`/`target_url` are its seed addresses.

target_list.description:
Replacement load-balancing target list for this version. An empty
list disables load balancing for the version, reverting it to its
effective `target_url`.

target_url.description:
Replacement upstream base URL for this version. Rejected at
validation time when the version's
effective `target_list` is non-empty — load-balanced traffic never
reads `target_url`, so the override would silently do nothing.

oneOf.description:
Replacement body transforms for this version (both rule lists and
the response cap — replaced wholesale).
Replacement header transforms for this version.

transform_method.description: Replacement method override for this version.

upstream_http2.description:
Replacement HTTP/2-upstream flag for this version (`false` reverts
the version to HTTP/1.1 upstream requests).

upstream_retries.description:
Replacement upstream retry count for this version (`0` disables
retries for the version).

upstream_timeout_ms.description: Replacement upstream timeout for this version.

url_rewrites.description: Replacement URL rewrite rules for this version.

VersioningConfig.description: Versioning settings for one API definition.

default_version.description:
Version used when the request names none. Unset means a version is
required: requests without one are rejected with `403`.

key.description:
The header or query-parameter name carrying the version. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_VERSION_KEY`].

location.description: Where the version name is read from. Defaults to a header.

versions.description: The versions this API serves, by name. Must not be empty.

tags.name: apis
tags.description: API definitions (storage source; live on reload)
